status: DRAFT 2026-11-14. The file format is a proposal. Items under 'decided' were settled by Brad on 14 Nov 2026; items under an entry's 'choices' are still open.
decided: A conflict that appears only over Cons is a third status, reported per default conclusion, not per graph.
Exceptions are read from the constraint statement in the graph.
An exception to a symmetric constraint is read on the subject of the statement, as the checker does.
Every constraint is an entry, whatever its status. The regime is the two P31/P279 rules.

format.term: A string. '?name' is a variable; anything else is a prefixed name from 'prefixes'.
format.triple: A list of three terms: subject, predicate, object.
format.conclusion: A triple, or the string 'BOT' for an incompatibility.
format.defeaters: A list of graphs, each a list of triples. The entry instance applies when its premises are in K and no defeater has an instance contained in K. Variables of a defeater that do not occur in the premises are existential.
format.guards: Comparisons between literals bound by the premises.
format.expand: The entry stands for one entry per listed value of the variable.
format.variant_of: Entries sharing this value are alternatives; exactly one is to be kept.

choices: Reading P31 and P279 as rdf:type and rdfs:subClassOf is ours. It is what the subject type constraint's relation 'instance of' (Q21503252) asks the checker to do.
Reading a symmetric-constraint violation as a default consequence is our stipulation; Wikidata documents constraints as hints for editors.
The defeater has the same form as on P47. The constraint statement on P26 lists no exception, so it has no instance today.

The entry applies when ?y is an unknown value (a Skolem IRI). No guard may exclude that case, since a guard may not depend on the identity of a Skolem term. The conclusion then has a Skolem IRI as subject. The checker reports compliance on such statements, so here the entry and the checker differ.

choices: Only date of birth and date of death are compared. The constraint is believed, from documentation, to use inception and start time, and dissolved and end time, as well.
Direct date values carry no precision, so a year-precision date appears as 1 January. Comparing them as written over-reports; comparing years only is the alternative.
When either date is absent the entry does not apply. The checker agrees: it reports compliance on three statements whose value has no dates.

The entry applies when some date of death precedes some date of birth. The checker compares the latest end with the earliest start, as its own message on Berta Gerster and Fritz Reiner says: it reports compliance on Elisabeth Magdalene von Brandenburg and Francis Otto, where one of two dates of death precedes the birth. Matching it would need a guard inside a defeater, which the format does not have.
The check has no direction, so the pair p26-contemporary-subject-first and p26-contemporary-value-first together express it. A violation is therefore present at K whichever direction is asserted.
